requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage kernel module from loading now
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed usb_storage was not loaded and no prior blacklist config existed (cmd-f7c4379e8591429d). Executor created /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with both 'blacklist usb-storage' and 'install usb-storage /bin/false' directives (cmd-df3c33bcaff9424b), then directly verified immediate enforcement: sudo modprobe usb-storage failed with exit 1 and the module remained absent from lsmod (cmd-49d2dee21dc5465a).

requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage kernel module from loading after a reboot
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id (dfdea52d-a1af-4d7b-803a-15f40ee9dd4e) was captured, a real restart was performed via systemctl reboot with acknowledgement (cmd-b85f0cff485f4afb), and a differing post-reboot boot_id (ea72b178-cd0b-4d90-adb9-c13dfaa3e2fc) was observed (cmd-4b9a14aa0f274bff), confirming the transition occurred. Post-reboot verification directly showed the blacklist config file persisted intact, usb_storage remained absent from lsmod, and modprobe usb-storage still failed identically (cmd-f34552f3a02d41a1). This constitutes a full pre-restart/restart/post-restart demonstration specific to the task's own outcome, satisfying the bounded-disruption evidence bar.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — blocking usb-storage from loading immediately and after a reboot — are directly and coherently demonstrated with pre/post evidence spanning a real reboot (differing boot IDs) and consistent module-blocking behavior before and after. The only concern is an unnecessary, though bounded and non-destructive, initramfs rebuild that the executor's own diagnostics proved was not needed for the fix.
limitations: No independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol beyond the single reboot performed for the task itself was described separately, though for this single-node task the task-driven reboot doubles as that evidence; no contradiction was found between the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots and the executor's own recorded boot IDs.
Lifecycle listening-sockets diff shows only PID changes for sshd/chronyd across the reboot, consistent with expected restart behavior and not a hygiene concern.

operational_hygiene.summary: One unnecessary state-changing mutation was identified: cmd-dc3b9d8caa49407d ran 'sudo dracut -f --regenerate-all', a full initramfs regeneration for the host. The executor's own subsequent investigation (cmd-e83c6bbeffc1436d, cmd-5465f7ff92cb4eb3) confirmed usb-storage was never embedded in the initramfs and that the on-disk /etc/modprobe.d config alone governs load behavior at every boot, meaning the initramfs rebuild had no causal role in satisfying the task and was only a 'defense-in-depth' exploratory step that proved superfluous. This mutation was retained (the regenerated initramfs image remains in place; it was not reverted), though it is bounded to a single, standard, non-destructive system operation. Post-executor lifecycle snapshots show no failed services and clean package-health both before and after (global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services, global:before_prepare:node1:package-health, global:after_executor:node1:failed-services, global:after_executor:node1:package-health), so the mutation caused no observable damage. All other state-changing actions (writing the blacklist config, the reboot itself) were directly tied to satisfying the material task outcomes.
